summary: Bench sheets for the Nimbravelle NM-12 precipitation-on-dilution follow-up ({{PRJ0112:project_id}}). The vehicle ladder records undiluted behavior at the target loading. The cosolvent-rich vehicle failed dilution and Nimbravelle selected dispersed dosing with explicit redispersion and withdrawal controls.

rows: Nimbravelle NM-12 oral vehicle: precipitation-on-dilution follow-up
The cosolvent-rich vehicle failed the dilution challenge. Nimbravelle selected a dispersed dosing approach.
Vehicle screen, Dilution check, Handling notes

sheets.name: Vehicle screen
rows: Solubility in mg/mL at equilibrium. Stability read at 24 h after loading at 10 mg/mL.

sheets.name: Dilution check
rows: PEG400/water was clear and stable in the initial screen; this did not establish dilution stability.
The cosolvent-rich vehicle failed the dilution challenge. Refer to the dilution bench records for vehicle identity, concentration, dilution ratios and observations.
Nimbravelle selected dispersed dosing. Refer to the selected recipe card for composition.
The undiluted table is not evidence of absence of precipitation after dilution.

sheets.name: Handling notes
rows: Final. Nimbravelle selected dispersed dosing after the cosolvent-rich vehicle failed dilution.

Redispersion and withdrawal controls must accompany the dosing recipe. Re-establish uniform dispersion before withdrawal and follow the source handling instructions; settling can change the dose withdrawn.
The HPMC/Tween screen showed crystal growth, and citrate buffer showed caking at 24 h. These rows do not establish clean diluted preparations.
